approvals.title: TICVAI — Approvals
approvals.tip: One approval mechanism, not five. Refund thresholds, shift variance, release promotion and manual discount were four bespoke implementations; a fifth was about to be written for AI. Approval records an authorisation and never performs the action.

ai.title: TICVAI — AI
ai.tip: Retrieval and inference over data the platform already holds. Nothing here needs a trained model — forecasting, fraud, dynamic pricing and recommendation are parked until there is a season of history. Two stores: Postgres for metadata, Qdrant for embeddings.

workforce.title: TICVAI — Workforce
workforce.tip: Rota, attendance and announcements — the three things the employee app needs that nothing owned. A rota assignment is not a shift: a shift is a cash session, and most people on a rota never touch a till.

access.tip: Admission. Access points, admission profiles, scan events. Partitioned by venue because scan volume dominates.

assets.tip: Media. Renamed from `asset` because it collided with maintenance assets.

catalogue.tip: What can be sold and how much of it exists. Products, variants, envelopes, leases and entitlement templates.

control.tip: The Control Plane. Cells, releases, migrations, licences. Lives outside every cell because it provisions them.

fnb.tip: Food and beverage. Menus, kitchen tickets, tables, delivery locations and guest self-ordering.

games.tip: Arcade and ride play, prize redemption.

identity.tip: Principals, roles, grants, SSO and MFA. Authorisation is user-driven, not workstation-driven (ADR-0002).

inventory.tip: Procurement and stock. Purchase orders, receipts, counts, transfers and par levels.

ledger.tip: Double-entry accounting. Append-only: a posted entry is reversed, never edited.

maintenance.tip: Assets, work orders, inspections and incidents. Safety-critical assets need verification by someone other than the person who did the work.

marketing.tip: CRM, segments, campaigns, consent and loyalty. Consent lives at tenant level because the controller is the tenant.

orders.tip: The commerce backbone. One order may carry a ticket, a locker, a meal and parking, each fulfilling differently.

pii.tip: Personal data, separately erasable. The only place a subject_id joins back to a person — which is why reporting reads a replica without it.

platform.tip: The spine. Scope tree, tenants, venues, workstations, devices and the outbox. Every scoped read resolves through here.

promotions.tip: Rules the platform evaluates, distinct from a manual discount a cashier chooses.

queue.tip: Virtual queues. Wait times come from a sensor, a vendor API, or a supervisor typing them — manual is a real adaptor.

reporting.tip: Report definitions, executions and dashboards. Reads the analytical replica, never the primary.

retail.tip: Merchandise, stock at outlet level, shop-and-drop.

seating.tip: Seat maps, categories, holds and blocks. The only module where two terminals can destroy each other.

sync.tip: Offline sync bookkeeping for POS and scanner.

whitelabel.tip: Tenant branding and module enablement. One app, one store listing, per ADR-0006.

approvals.tip: The shared approval object. Four rules are not configurable: a requester never approves their own request, a rejection carries a reason, a completed record is immutable, and approval authorises without executing.

workforce.tip: Who is expected where, who actually turned up, and what staff have been told. The gap between the first two is the operational value of having both.

control.cell_cluster.tip: identical cells serving a region. Scaling out is launching another, not growing one

control.tenant_migration.tip: a tenant moving between cells — shared to dedicated, or rebalancing

control.tenant_migration_plan.tip: computed against cell state; expires, because a plan made for a different world is not a plan

fnb.delivery_location_outlet.tip: join table. Which outlets serve which locations

fnb.location_code.tip: rotating location codes, hashed and time-bounded

fnb.menu.tip: A menu belongs to a venue and an outlet is assigned one (ADR-0018). Sections and items hang beneath it.

fnb.recipe.tip: What a menu item consumes. The link between selling a burger and depleting stock.

games.game.tip: An arcade or ride unit. Bound to a maintenance asset, so a game goes out of service when its asset does — and back only when verified.

identity.authz_audit.tip: written by the platform, read through reporting

identity.principal_credential.tip: a credential hash has no response it belongs in

ledger.fx_rate.tip: configured rates with effective windows. A rate change is a new row; the old is never edited

ledger.inter_entity_obligation.tip: what one legal entity owes another after a cross-region redemption

orders.no_sale_event.tip: drawer opened without a sale. Recorded because it is the classic cover for theft

orders.order_discount.tip: manual discount with reason and approver. Posts to a discount account, never as a price change

orders.order_media_link.tip: links an order to the media its entitlements were issued onto. What makes append-to-existing possible without editing a paid order

orders.payment_tip.tip: tips post to a liability, not to sales

pii.subject.tip: Derived from storage only — no contract schema.

pii.subject_biometric.tip: Derived from storage only — no contract schema.

pii.subject_contact.tip: Derived from storage only — no contract schema.

pii.subject_document.tip: Derived from storage only — no contract schema.

platform.outbox.tip: transactional outbox. Events have contracts; the row does not

platform.tenant.tip: read-only projection of control.tenant, outside every cell

sync.rejection.tip: What an offline terminal sent that the server refused. The queue a supervisor works through after an outage, and the reason offline sync is not fire-and-forget.

approvals.request.tip: One request per action needing authorisation. The subject is a reference, never a copy

approvals.decision.tip: Every decision at every level. **Immutable once the request completes** — an approval is evidence

approvals.matrix.tip: What requires approval where. Versioned, because a request must be decided by the rules it was raised under

approvals.rule.tip: Ordered within a matrix. First match wins, so adding a rule cannot silently change another

approvals.delegation.tip: Standing in for an approver. Always time-bounded — an open-ended delegation is one nobody remembers

approvals.escalation.tip: Who was asked, when, and why it moved up. The original approver stays in the record

ai.chunk_ref.tip: Maps a Qdrant point id back to its document and scope. **The join between the two stores**

ai.conversation.tip: A thread, scoped to a principal and a module. **Analytical store, not the transactional primary** (ADR-0020) — append-only with an analytical read pattern, and it must not compete with a gate scan for a connection.

ai.index_entry.tip: Maps a source row to its Qdrant point ids, so a deletion in Postgres can be followed into the vector store. **Nothing cascades between the two**

ai.index_job.tip: A build in flight. recordsFailed is the number to watch — a source failing on 3% of rows is a search missing 3% of answers

ai.index_source.tip: One declaration per indexed table. The owning service does not know it exists — the AI service consumes the event that service already publishes

ai.interaction.tip: The audit record. **Retention is unresolved (CF-64)** — a prompt may carry personal data. **Analytical store, not the transactional primary** (ADR-0020) — append-only with an analytical read pattern, and it must not compete with a gate scan for a connection.

ai.knowledge_collection.tip: A collection in the vector store. **One per embedding model** — a collection carries its own vector config and a shard cannot, so two models cannot share one (ADR-0021). Carries the shard key, which is the tenant boundary on shared placement

ai.knowledge_document.tip: Source, status and chunk count. The text and its vectors live in Qdrant

ai.message.tip: Prompt and response with sources, provider, model, tokens and latency. **Analytical store, not the transactional primary** (ADR-0020) — append-only with an analytical read pattern, and it must not compete with a gate scan for a connection.

ai.policy.tip: What the assistant may do, which roles may use it, what is masked. Resolves tenant then venue (ADR-0018)

ai.proposed_action.tip: A draft the assistant produced and a person must approve. Nothing executes from here

ai.provider.tip: Configured providers, models and failover order. Credentials are a vault reference, never a key

control.release.tip: a shipped version. Promoted through dev, staging and production; superseded by a later one

games.credit_ledger.tip: credits bought, played and won. The arcade equivalent of a wallet

identity.guest_session.tip: a guest session. Separate from staff — different lifetime, different auth

identity.mfa_challenge.tip: an issued MFA challenge and its outcome

identity.otp_challenge.tip: a one-time code sent to a guest contact point

identity.session.tip: a staff session, carrying the workstation and the selected role

inventory.stock_level.tip: quantity on hand per item per location. **Gates the sale at outlet level** (14 August)

marketing.message_delivery.tip: one row per recipient per send. Delivery, bounce and engagement

orders.cash_count_line.tip: a denomination and a count from a blind till count

orders.credit_override.tip: a manual override of a partner credit limit, recorded with who and why. Second table on a marker the deriver only read the first half of

reporting.report_field.tip: the fields a report definition may use. Retrievable, so a report can be found by what it answers

maintenance.work_order_attachment.tip: Photo, video, document, note or signature against a work order. Evidence, not decoration — captured offline and queued

workforce.announcement.tip: Targeted by venue, department or role. `emergency` is not a louder `operational`

workforce.announcement_receipt.tip: Delivered and acknowledged, per principal. **The outstanding list is the roll call**

workforce.attendance.tip: Who actually turned up. **occurredAt and recordedAt are both kept** — a steward clocking in offline is not late because the sync was

workforce.rota_assignment.tip: A person expected somewhere at a time. **Not a shift** — a shift is a cash session, and most people on a rota never touch a till

workforce.shift_swap.tip: Both parties agree before the supervisor sees it. Routed through approvals rather than a second mechanism

promotions.bundle_choice_group.tip: Pick n from a set. The bundle price does not move with the choice (ADR-0019) — the allocation does

platform.audit_read.tip: **PII reads only.** Who looked at a passport number is the question a regulator asks, and auditing every read produces a log nobody can search

platform.audit_record.tip: One row per write. Who, what, when, from where, under which permission, and the before and after. **occurredAt and recordedAt are both kept** — an offline action happened when it happened

catalogue.donation_campaign.tip: Fixed, free or round-up. **Posts to a liability account, not revenue** — money collected for a charity is not the venue’s to recognise

catalogue.waitlist_entry.tip: Who asked to be told when a sold-out session frees up. **Not a queue** — a queue is people standing at a ride

fnb.table_reservation.tip: A booking with a time and a party size. Distinct from a table session, which is a guest already sitting down

orders.cart.tip: A cart holds leases; an order holds money. Retained after expiry so a recovery link lands on something

orders.cart_line.tip: One line, with the lease that holds its capacity. Null lease for a product with no capacity

orders.donation_line.tip: A donation within a transaction. A line, not a flag, because one transaction may give to several campaigns

access.parking_entitlement.tip: A guest bought parking. Carries the plate where the mode is plateWhitelist — **personal data**, since a plate identifies a person

access.parking_facility.tip: A car park and its integration mode. Three modes, and the mode decides what happens at sale (CF-52)

control.partner_agreement.tip: Net rate or commission, credit terms, validity. **Versioned** — an order placed last week used last week’s rate

ai.layout_draft.tip: A generated seat layout awaiting review. **Ends at previewReady and writes nothing to the seat map** — the draft enters seating.import_job at its existing human commit step (ADR-0020)

qdrant:knowledge.tip: **One collection per embedding model** (ADR-0021) — a collection is the only Qdrant container that can carry its own vector configuration, and a shard cannot. Tenants sharing a model share this collection, separated by shard key and scope_path payload; a tenant forced onto a local model by residency

orders.deposit_box.tip: A cashier’s cash box. **Allocated to a person, not a workstation** — a cashier moving between tills takes their float, which is what makes a variance attributable. withdrawnTotal reduces the expected close: cash skimmed for banking is not a shortfall

marketing.agent_availability.tip: Available, busy, away or offline, with a concurrency limit. **Expires** — an agent who forgets to go offline is one conversations queue for

marketing.conversation.tip: A live session with somebody waiting. **Not a case** — a case is a ticket measured in hours, this is measured in seconds. A conversation may create a case; it is not one

marketing.conversation_message.tip: One message. The sender is resolved, never declared, and **the assistant is labelled as one** — a guest talking to a bot that presents as a person is a complaint waiting to happen

marketing.kiosk_assist_session.tip: A staff member acting on a kiosk session remotely (2.1.25). **The guest can always see it and always end it** — assistance a guest cannot stop is surveillance

cache:answer.tip: **Question, scope and locale to an answer.** The largest cost lever at a kiosk, where forty questions repeat thousands of times a day. **Invalidated by the same events that invalidate the index** — a cached answer that outlives a price change has misled a guest on the venue’s behalf. **`scope_path`

cache:embedding.tip: Content hash and model to a vector. **A tenant editing fifty of twenty thousand chunks re-embeds fifty.** Invalidation is trivial because the key changes when the content does

cache:idempotency.tip: Seen idempotency keys. **Every write carries one as of 17 August and nothing said where the record lived or how long it was kept** — a key store that forgets too early lets a replay through, which is the defect the key exists to prevent. Retention must exceed the longest offline window (ADR-0013) **

cache:resolution.tip: Scope and permission resolution, tenant configuration, price lists. **Read on every request and changed rarely** — `resolvePermissions` reads five tables on every authorised call

0001.title: Cell architecture — one tenant per jurisdiction
0001.tip: **Superseded** by ADR-0014 and ADR-0017. Kept for its Context and Alternatives. Do not cite its Decision section — reasoning from it produced a cross-tenant isolation defect on 17 August (CF-97).

0002.title: Authorisation is user-driven, not workstation-driven
0002.tip: **Authorisation is user/role-driven. A user logs in from any device and carries their access.**

0003.title: Conditional role selection at login
0003.tip: **One role → direct login. Several roles → selection prompt.** Confirmed 12 Aug 2026 §4 and corroborated by the reference system's own behaviour.

0004.title: Single session per user
0004.tip: **Single session per user.** A second login is **rejected**, not auto-terminating the first. A supervisor holding `SESSION_FORCE_LOGOUT` may terminate an abandoned session.

0005.title: Venue isolation by partitioning, not separate databases
0005.tip: **Venues are isolated by Postgres list partitioning on `venue_id`**, within the tenant database. Not separate databases.

0006.title: Tiered guest app distribution
0006.tip: **Tiered (Option C).** Dedicated and isolated tenants get branded native apps published under **their own** Apple and Google accounts, with TICVAI granted App Manager access. Shared-tier tenants get a branded PWA. A universal TICVAI app exists as a discovery surface only.

0007.title: Hybrid repository topology
0007.tip: **Polyrepo between runtimes, monorepo within frontend.** Six repositories: contracts, backend, frontend, ai, infra, docs.

0008.title: Money carries per-region scale
0008.tip: Money is `{ amount, currency, scale }` at every layer. SQL columns are `numeric(18,4)` with the currency and scale carried alongside. Wire format is a decimal **string**, never a float.

0009.title: AI Data Residency
0009.tip: **Residency is an architectural property, not a storage location.** TICVAI keeps the entire AI processing path in-jurisdiction by default, and treats any cross-border path as an Article 22/23 transfer requiring a documented mechanism.

0010.title: Cross-Jurisdiction Entitlements
0010.tip: **Home-cell ownership with delegated redemption.** No shared database, no distributed transaction, and no personal data crossing a border without a basis.

0011.title: The Hierarchy Is Binding
0011.tip: **The hierarchy is binding. Only the example populating it was illustrative.**

0013.title: Local-First Point of Sale
0013.tip: **Local-first. One read path, always local, online or offline.**

0015.title: Standards-First Device Drivers
0015.tip: **Classify every device class by whether a standard exists, and treat the three tiers differently.**

0016.title: — Read and write paths are separated, and routing is declared per operation
0016.tip: **Every operation declares which database it reads, in `x-ticvai-read-routing`.** Three values, and the routing layer refuses to serve an operation whose declaration it cannot satisfy.

0017.title: — Deployment models
0017.tip: **Four deployment models. One is the default; the others exist because a client asked or a law requires it.**

0018.title: — Configuration scope
0018.tip: **Configuration resolves up the scope tree. Nearest ancestor wins. There are three levels.**

0019.title: A dynamic bundle has a fixed price and a variable allocation
0019.tip: The guest picks; the total does not move. Allocation across the chosen components is proportional to list price at sale and frozen on the order line.

0020.title: Where AI runs, and what it is isolated from
0020.tip: Retrieval and the index stay in the cell; inference is a call out and only the prompt leaves; the AI logs move off the transactional primary. ADR-0009 answered the legal question and never this one.

0021.title: Qdrant — one collection per embedding model, tenant is the shard, scope is the filter
0021.tip: The split criterion is the embedding model, not the tenant — a shard inherits the collection vector config and cannot differ. Tenants share a collection, separated by shard and payload; residency-forced local models get their own.

0022.title: Conflict policy is declared per operation, from a closed set of four

0024.title: The contract is the deliverable, and it is written before anything else

check-screens.tip: Component vocabulary, operation ids, required states, navigation resolution, and platform naming — audience against surface, form factor against runtime. Fails a POS or handheld that is not offline-capable.

check-frontend.tip: App existence, route uniqueness, component path convention, and that offline-capable apps declare the offline-core package.

check-flows.tip: Every flow step names a screen that exists and an operation that exists, and the step sequence agrees with the declared navigation edges.

check-states.tip: Every enum value is modelled, every state reachable, every state reaches a terminal one, every named operation exists, and every emitted event is catalogued. Also fails a path key declared twice — YAML keeps the last and drops the first, silently.

check-config-scope.tip: Every configuration operation declares its level, nothing configures below venue, and a config scope never sits below the caller scope. ADR-0018.

check-migrations.tip: Dormant while no DDL exists. RLS with FORCE, level-typed foreign keys, money types, rollback blocks, reference existence, and Postgres enums matching their contract counterparts.

build-cf-index.tip: Regenerates the conflict index and the register summary from the rows, because a count kept by hand beside the thing it counts will drift — and did.

link-screens-contracts.tip: Derives both directions: which screens consume an operation, and which operations a screen calls.

contracts.tip: 642 OpenAPI operations across 22 files. Eight spine contracts other modules depend on, fourteen satellites that depend on the spine and never on each other.

schema workbook.tip: 232 tables and 2,026 columns, derived from persistence markers on the contracts. Regenerated whenever contracts change. This is the working artefact while no DDL exists.

storage-design.tip: The 30% of a migration that does not derive from the contracts — RLS, level-typed foreign keys, partitioning, indexes, constraints, functions.

screens.tip: 180 definitions across 8 platforms. Each carries purpose, capability, wave, API calls, layout regions, states including offline, navigation and implementation path.

states.tip: 20 state models. Enums declare what states exist; these declare which moves between them are legal.

events.tip: 16 domain events. What goes through platform.outbox — publisher, consumers, payload, and every consumer declaring its idempotency key.

flows.tip: 5 user journeys with their unhappy paths. Each one written has found a missing screen.

conflict register.tip: 72 conflicts with the full reasoning behind each. conflict-status.md is the generated index.

relationships.csv.tip: 406 table relationships with an edge_kind: ambient points at a hub and says nothing about this table, child means this row belongs to that row, reference is a real relationship.

audit-register.tip: Every write operation is auditable. The register says what is recorded by default and which subset needs more — money, access, PII, permissions, AI, approvals and configuration.

notification-catalogue.tip: Event to audience to channel to consent. The three silences are decisions, listed so a reader can tell decided-against from forgotten.

ai-index.tip: Where every AI artefact lives. AI has no folder — the package is organised by artefact kind — so this is the index that replaces one.

ai-credentials.tip: One provider key per tenant, optionally per venue. No surface ever holds one — every surface calls TICVAI and TICVAI calls the provider.

cell.tip: One isolated deployment. Four kinds: shared (many tenants, RLS), dedicated (one tenant), on-premise (the venue hardware) and the Control Plane. ADR-0017.

scope_node.tip: The hierarchy as one ltree table — tenant, brand, region, venue, department, sub-department, workstation. There is no separate venue table, deliberately.

scope_path.tip: An ltree column carried on scoped rows. The RLS predicate walks it, which is why every ltree column has a GiST index.

RLS FORCE.tip: Without FORCE the table owner bypasses every policy. On a shared cell RLS is the only thing between two paying customers.

lease.tip: Capacity allocated to a terminal so it can sell offline. Expires automatically — a terminal that dies must not strand its allocation.

entitlement.tip: A right to admission, a meal, a locker. Issued by an order and appendable to media the guest already holds (CF-58).

media.tip: What the guest carries — QR, wristband, card. Several entitlements may share one, which is why appending is keyed on media rather than order.

outbox.tip: Events written in the same transaction as the state change, so a crash cannot leave an event unpublished for a change that happened.

idempotency key.tip: What makes a redelivery a duplicate. Required on every event consumer, because at-least-once delivery makes this the difference between a correct consumer and one that works until it does not.

blind count.tip: The expected figure is withheld until the count is submitted. A counter who can see the expected total reconciles to it rather than to the drawer.

spine and satellite.tip: A satellite may depend on the spine. A satellite never depends on another satellite — that rule is what stops the contract set becoming a graph nobody can reason about.

wave.tip: 1 is the first release, 2 follows. A Wave 1 surface cannot wait on a Wave 2 dependency, which is what CF-41 and the Accreditation workshop are about.

approval matrix.tip: Rules resolving up the scope tree — tenant default, region override, venue override. First match wins, and a venue may tighten a threshold and never loosen one.

segregation of duties.tip: A requester may never approve their own request, and delegation does not create a way around it.

rota assignment.tip: A person expected somewhere at a time. Distinct from a shift, which is a cash session tied to a workstation.

F01.name: Guest buys a ticket online
F01.tip: A guest arrives wanting to visit. Most arrive on a product page from a search engine or a campaign link rather than the homepage, so the flow must work from any entry point.

F02.name: Guest buys seated tickets
F02.tip: A guest choosing a specific seat rather than general admission.

F03.name: Partner books on credit
F03.tip: A reseller booking against an agreed credit line rather than paying up front.

F04.name: Platform admin ships a release
F04.tip: A release is ready to move from staging to production across every cell.

F05.name: Agent resolves a guest complaint
F05.tip: A guest contacts support about an order.

F06.name: Guest enters the venue
F06.tip: A guest presents a ticket, wristband or phone at a gate. This runs tens of thousands of times a day and is the flow with the least tolerance for latency.

F07.name: Guest buys at a kiosk
F07.tip: A guest at the entrance chooses to buy from a machine rather than queue for a counter. Nobody is standing beside them, which changes every failure.

F08.name: Steward works a shift on the employee app
F08.tip: A member of venue staff arrives for a shift and works through it on their phone.

F09.name: Event is cancelled and refunded
F09.tip: A performance is cancelled — weather, a technical failure, an artist. Every ticket sold for it needs handling, and the guests need telling before they travel.

F10.name: Partner books, uses and settles
F10.tip: A tour operator books a block, distributes vouchers to their customers, those customers arrive over weeks, and at month end the two businesses reconcile.

F11.name: Guest orders food to a lounger
F11.tip: A guest on a sunbed opens the app, scans the QR on their lounger, orders, and a runner brings it. Described in detail by the client on 14 August.

F12.name: Asset fails and closes a queue
F12.tip: A ride stops. A technician is dispatched, works on it, and it returns to service — or does not. The guest app must stop advertising a queue for a ride nobody can board.

F13.name: Month end closes
F13.tip: The month has ended and the books must be closed before anyone reports on them.

F14.name: A discount needs a manager
F14.tip: A cashier applies a discount larger than their own authority, with a guest standing at the counter.

F15.name: A part is needed and ordered
F15.tip: A technician opens a machine, finds the fault, and the part is not on the shelf.

F16.name: A venue opens for the first time
F16.tip: A tenant has signed and a venue must exist before anyone can configure or sell anything.

F17.name: A guest buys merchandise and collects later
F17.tip: A guest buys something at a shop and does not want to carry it around the park all day (4.4.7).

F18.name: A guest plays an arcade game
F18.tip: A guest taps a game card on a machine and plays.

F19.name: A membership works in another country
F19.tip: A guest bought an annual pass in Dubai and arrives at a venue in Abu Dhabi, in a different cell because data residency put it there.

F20.name: A manager asks a question and gets an answer
F20.tip: A venue manager wants to know something the platform knows and does not want to find the report.

F21.name: A ride queue fills and a guest is redirected
F21.tip: A guest opens the app to decide what to do next, and the ride they wanted has an hour's wait.

F22.name: A tenant rebrands their app
F22.tip: A venue changes its logo, colours and homepage, and it must reach the website and the app without a release.

F23.name: A contractor gets a badge and uses it
F23.tip: A contractor needs access to a plant room for a week, and a steward at a service gate must be able to check it.
